item.title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79487-5

More redundancy doesn’t always mean more resilience. Here, the authors use seven-year-long metagenomics data from soils above Centralia’s coal seam fire to show that heat disturbance increases microbial functional redundancy but narrows environmental responsiveness, potentially lowering insurance against future stress.
item.dc:title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
item.dc:creator: Samuel E. Barnett
Ashley Shade

item.title: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as saturated bioisosteres of meta-benzene
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79402-y

The authors synthesize bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes and provide support for their ability to mimic meta-substituted benzenes in biological contexts.
item.dc:title: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as saturated bioisosteres of meta-benzene

item.title: Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78715-2

The authors introduce CPAM-LLM, a framework that converts unstructured optimization problems into executable constraint models using LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, data augmentation, and dynamic constraints.
item.dc:title: Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI

item.title: In vivo programming of dual-targeted CAR-T cells facilitates vascular disruption and T-cell infiltration in solid tumors
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79342-7

Li and colleagues introduce an mRNA lipid nanoparticle platform for the selective transfection of endogenous T cells within the spleen; by dual-targeted CAR T cell in vivo programming, the authors show that VEGFR2 CAR-T cells disrupt the tumor vasculature, favoring the infiltration and activity of tumor-directed CAR-T cells.
item.dc:title: In vivo programming of dual-targeted CAR-T cells facilitates vascular disruption and T-cell infiltration in solid tumors

item.title: Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BO<sub>x</sub> catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79394-9

Oxidative dehydrogenation of propane (ODHP) offers a promising route to propylene, but developing catalysts that operate efficiently at low temperatures while maintaining high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, the authors report a Co@BOx inverse catalyst in which phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter enable efficient low-temperature ODHP.
item.dc:title: Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BO<sub>x</sub> catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation

item.title: Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79710-3

This work develops a Ce-assisted strategy to build 3D oxygen-diffusion scaffolds in Al fuels, overcoming Al2O3 diffusion barriers and achieving complete oxidation and enhanced combustion.
item.dc:title: Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels

item.title: Atomically ordered few-layer molybdenum boride MBenes for enhanced electromagnetic response
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79512-7

The authors develop a theory-guided molten-salt route that selectively removes aluminum to produce atomically ordered, few-layer MoB MBenes with few Mo vacancies. The preserved Mo−B framework enhances polarization and electromagnetic response.
item.dc:title: Atomically ordered few-layer molybdenum boride MBenes for enhanced electromagnetic response

item.title: Asymmetric coordination triggers dual-site synergy in gold nanoclusters for efficient aerobic oxidation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79369-w

The construction of atomically precise heterogeneous catalysts that integrate multiple distinct active sites into a synergistic architecture is highly attractive but challenging. Here, we report an Au39 nanocluster with heteroatoms introduced to modulate the local coordination environment and construct asymmetric coordination units on the surface.
item.dc:title: Asymmetric coordination triggers dual-site synergy in gold nanoclusters for efficient aerobic oxidation

item.title: Facial photographs reveal mortality risk beyond triage and clinical risk scores
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79581-8

Using 27,660 smartphone facial photos, researchers showed that the facial appearance from emergency admission predicts mortality and high-risk patients better than triage, early warning scores, vitals, or lab tests.
item.dc:title: Facial photographs reveal mortality risk beyond triage and clinical risk scores

item.title: A dual-anchoring mechanism for hemimethylated CG-guided histone ubiquitylation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79633-z

VIM proteins regulate maintenance of plant CG methylation. Here the authors show how the interaction of VIM1 with hemimethylated linker DNA and the acidic patch of a nucleosome governs its histone ubiquitylation activity for maintenance of DNA methylation.
item.dc:title: A dual-anchoring mechanism for hemimethylated CG-guided histone ubiquitylation

item.title: Protecting-group-lean platform for synthesizing diverse phenylethanoid glycosides uncovers antifibrotic leads
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79652-w

Phenylethanoid glycosides constitute one of the most structurally diverse classes of natural glycosides, yet systematic investigation is constrained by limited access to preparative quantities. Here, the authors report a protecting group-lean platform that delivers a 29-member library of phenylethanoid glycosides.
item.dc:title: Protecting-group-lean platform for synthesizing diverse phenylethanoid glycosides uncovers antifibrotic leads
